question: A team is documenting the SSE event flow for the Messages API streaming endpoint so that other engineers can build custom parsers. Which of the following statements about the event flow are accurate? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) ping events occur at a fixed interval of exactly one per content block and never appear at any other point in the stream.
B) Each content block is bounded by a content_block_start event and a content_block_stop event, with zero or more content_block_delta events in between.
C) A single stream can only contain one content block; content_block_start and content_block_stop therefore each appear exactly once per stream.
D) Each stream begins with a message_start event containing a Message object whose content array is empty.
E) message_delta events report top-level changes to the Message object, such as stop_reason, and one or more message_delta events can be sent before the final message_stop event.
F) The stream always ends with a message_stop event, which is sent before the final message_delta event so that clients can start finalizing usage totals early.
correct_answers: B) Each content block is bounded by a content_block_start event and a content_block_stop event, with zero or more content_block_delta events in between.
D) Each stream begins with a message_start event containing a Message object whose content array is empty.
E) message_delta events report top-level changes to the Message object, such as stop_reason, and one or more message_delta events can be sent before the final message_stop event.
explanations: Incorrect — ping events can appear any number of times throughout the stream and are not tied to a fixed per-content-block interval.
Correct — every content block follows the pattern of a start event, zero or more deltas, and a stop event.
Incorrect — a stream can contain multiple content blocks (for example, text followed by a tool_use block), each with its own start/stop pair and distinct index.
Correct — message_start is the first event and carries a Message object with an empty content array, to be filled in as the stream progresses.
Correct — message_delta communicates top-level changes such as stop_reason and cumulative usage, and one or more of these events can precede the final message_stop.
Incorrect — message_stop is the final event in the stream, sent after all message_delta events, not before them.
